en: The Legend of the Elder Sāgata Kuṇḍadhāna Chapter, Number Two I was a young brahmin, well-versed in the Vedas, and I dwelt in the city of Benares. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, was staying at the Deer Park in Isipatana near Benares. Having heard of his fame, I went to him with a retinue of five hundred. Upon seeing the Blessed One, my heart was filled with joy; I paid homage to him and sat down to one side. As I sat there, the Blessed One, out of compassion for me, gave me a Dhamma talk. Having heard that Dhamma talk, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. Then, having taken refuge in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha, I took up the training rules and became a lay follower. After some time, I fell ill and was afflicted by a severe disease. While I was lying on my back, suffering and tormented by pain, I thought: "It would be good if I could see the Blessed One while I am still alive. Then the Blessed One, knowing with his own mind the reflection in my mind, approached me. Seeing the Blessed One from afar, I was overjoyed and said to him: "Venerable sir, may the Blessed One come to me; it will be for my long-term welfare and happiness. The Blessed One consented by remaining silent. He then approached me and sat down on the prepared seat. As he sat there, I paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One, understanding my state of mind, taught me the Dhamma in such a way that, having heard it, I attained the fruit of non-returning. When I had passed away from that life, I was reborn in the Tusita heaven. There, I lived for the full lifespan of the devas, enjoying celestial pleasures. After passing away from there, I was reborn in the human world in the city of Sāvatthī. There, I was born into a wealthy family, endowed with great wealth and possessions. When I grew up, I entered the monastic order under the Blessed One. Through diligent effort, I developed the four bases of psychic power and attained mastery over them. I then performed various miracles: I walked upon the water as if on dry land, I passed through solid ground as if through water, and I traveled through the air like a bird on the wing. I even emitted fire and water from my body. Having displayed these manifold wonders, I went to the Blessed One and paid homage to him. The Blessed One, seeing me, spoke these words: "Sāgata, you have indeed performed many wonders; you have truly become a wonder-worker. Hearing this, I was filled with joy and said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, I have not performed any wonders; rather, it is through the power of the Blessed One’s teaching that I have attained these states. The Blessed One then praised me in the midst of the assembly: "Monks, this monk Sāgata is one who has attained the four bases of psychic power and has mastery over them. Hearing this, the monks were delighted and paid homage to me. Thus did I dwell in the presence of the Blessed One, honored and respected. Through the merit of those deeds, I have now been reborn in the realm of the Thirty-three gods. Here, I enjoy the splendor of the devas, surrounded by a host of celestial maidens. My divine form is radiant and beautiful, and I dwell in the company of the noble ones. May I always encounter Buddhas, and may I never be separated from the True Dhamma. May I always be devoted to the Saṅgha, and may I never fall away from the holy life. May I attain the goal of all asceticism, and may I reach the end of suffering.

May I always be a refuge for beings, and may I lead them across the ocean of saṃsāra. May I always be a light in the darkness, and may I illuminate the world with the light of wisdom. May I always be a protector for the helpless, and may I bring comfort to those who are suffering. May I always be a friend to the lonely, and may I dispel the fear of those who are afraid. May I always be a teacher of the Dhamma, and may I lead beings to the deathless state. May I always be a vessel of compassion, and may I never abandon the practice of loving-kindness. May I always be a field of merit for the world, and may I receive the offerings of the faithful. May I always be a source of inspiration, and may I encourage others toward the path of liberation. May I always be a lamp in the darkness, and may I dispel the gloom of ignorance. May I always be a boat for those crossing, and may I carry them safely to the further shore. May I always be a bridge for those wandering, and may I help them cross over the river of saṃsāra. May I always be a shelter for those seeking rest, and may I provide relief to those who are weary. May I always be a guide for the lost, and may I show the way to those who wander in confusion. May I always be a healer for the sick, and may I cure the ailments of those who suffer. May I always be a provider of food for the hungry, and may I satisfy the needs of those who are famished. May I always be a giver of water to the thirsty, and may I quench the thirst of those who are parched. May I always be a giver of clothing to the naked, and may I clothe those who are destitute. May I always be a giver of medicine to the ill, and may I provide healing for those who are diseased. May I always be a giver of wealth to the poor, and may I relieve the suffering of those who are indigent. May I always be a giver of safety to the fearful, and may I grant protection to those who are in danger. May I always be a giver of peace to the agitated, and may I bring tranquility to those who are troubled. May I always be a giver of joy to the sorrowful, and may I dispel the grief of those who are weeping. May I always be a giver of hope to the despondent, and may I inspire confidence in those who are discouraged. May I always be a giver of strength to the weak, and may I empower those who are frail. May I always be a giver of courage to the timid, and may I instill bravery in those who are fearful. May I always be a giver of wisdom to the ignorant, and may I bestow knowledge upon those who are deluded. May I always be a giver of virtue to the immoral, and may I lead the unrighteous to the path of righteousness. May I always be a giver of patience to the angry, and may I teach forbearance to those who are wrathful. May I always be a giver of truth to the deceitful, and may I establish honesty in those who are dishonest. May I always be a giver of generosity to the stingy, and may I encourage liberality in those who are greedy. May I always be a giver of kindness to the cruel, and may I inspire compassion in those who are harsh. May I always be a giver of mercy to the merciless, and may I extend pity to those who are heartless. May I always be a giver of love to the hateful, and may I foster affection in those who are hostile. May I always be a giver of friendship to the solitary, and may I offer companionship to those who are alone. May I always be a giver of support to the needy, and may I assist those who are in want. May I always be a giver of encouragement to the weary, and may I uplift those who are exhausted. May I always be a giver of inspiration to the faint-hearted, and may I rouse the spirits of those who are disheartened. May I always be a giver of guidance to the confused, and may I direct those who are lost. May I always be a giver of instruction to the unlearned, and may I teach those who are ignorant. May I always be a giver of counsel to the foolish, and may I advise those who lack discernment. May I always be a giver of example to the imitators, and may I serve as a model for those who follow. May I always be a giver of testimony to the doubters, and may I provide proof for those who are skeptical. May I always be a giver of proof to the unbelievers, and may I convince those who are faithless. May I always be a giver of assurance to the anxious, and may I grant certainty to those who are uncertain. May I always be a giver of stability to the wavering, and may I provide firm ground for those who are unsteady. May I always be a giver of endurance to the impatient, and may I teach perseverance to those who are quick-tempered. May I always be a giver of fortitude to the fragile, and may I strengthen those who are vulnerable. May I always be a giver of resilience to the broken, and may I restore the spirit of those who are shattered. May I always be a giver of renewal to the ruined, and may I bring about the recovery of those who are fallen. May I always be a giver of rebirth to the dead, and may I lead the deceased to a happy destination. May I always be a giver of life
“At that time, there was a brahmin named Sobhita by name;
he was preceded by his disciples.”
I went to the monastery.
At that time, the Blessed One was seated in front of the community of monks.
Having emerged from the gate of the park,
the Supreme Person stood there;
I beheld that Fully Awakened One.
With my teeth set against my teeth,
having calmed my own mind,
I praised the Leader of the World.
Whatever trees there are,
all of them grow upon the earth;
likewise, sentient beings possess intelligence.
They take root in the teaching of the Jina.
You are a wise caravan leader,
O Great Seer, for many people.
Having pulled one out of the wrong path,
you point out the right path;
tamed yourself, surrounded by those who are tamed.
With those who meditate and delight in meditation,
who are ardent and resolute,
peaceful and steadfast.
Adorned by assemblies,
you shine with merit and wisdom;
your radiance streams forth.
Just as at the rising of the sun,
the Great Seer Padumuttara, seeing her heart full of serene faith, [spoke].
Standing before the community of bhikkhus,
the Teacher spoke these verses:
“He who, having brought forth laughter...”
The brahmin praised me;
for a hundred thousand aeons he will delight in the world of the gods.
Having passed away from Tusita,
impelled by the root of merit,
[he was born] for the Blessed One Gotama.
He will go forth in the Teaching.
By that well-performed deed,
he will attain arahantship.
"By name he shall be known as Sāgata,
a disciple of the Teacher.
Having gone forth in body,
I avoided evil deeds;
having abandoned verbal misconduct,
I purified my livelihood.
Dwelling thus,
skilled in the fire element,
having fully understood all taints—
I dwell free from taints.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Sāgata spoke these verses.
This is the second legend of the elder Sāgata.
